# Ensembl 116 regression fixtures

[`ensembl116.gff3`](ensembl116.gff3) contains 232 unchanged feature rows from
25 complete gene models in the human Ensembl release 116 GRCh38.p14 annotation.
Gene IDs, coordinates, strands, feature types, parent links, tags, and all other
attributes are preserved. Only record selection and ordering have changed.
Unrelated `biological_region` rows are omitted. The original build metadata
and sequence-region directives for the selected chromosomes are retained.

The fixture contains all 16 transcript feature types observed in the full
source file. It includes DDX11L1, WASH7P, OR4G4P, OR4G11P, IGLV4-69, IGLJ1,
and IGLC1, as well as nearby DDX11L16 and ENSG00000290826 and small models for
the remaining transcript families. Selection uses gene IDs because symbols
such as WASH7P and DDX11L16 identify several distinct genes in this release.

The tests cover canonical TSSs and promoters, exon/CDS parent resolution,
introns, canonical versus all-transcript selection, and equivalent record
output through automatic preparation, existing CSI, and existing TBI indexes.
Both plain-text and ordinary gzip preparation are exercised. Test variants
are synthetic position probes; the gene annotations are authentic provider
records. No download is required to run these tests.

## Sources

The full source is
[`Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gff3.gz`](https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-116/gff3/homo_sapiens/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gff3.gz),
with SHA-256:

```text
08e881d96ab6385a2c31f063a018be4b2c36860b323f2724be07022deeef21ce
```

The IGLV4-69, IGLJ1, and IGLC1 models were also checked against
[`Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.chromosome.22.gff3.gz`](https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-116/gff3/homo_sapiens/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.chromosome.22.gff3.gz),
with SHA-256:

```text
5f7d3b2dc44a4fa77c0f395be359510a00490932fbcdda667f8da26a2d42a857
```

Their feature rows match exactly between the two source files. Both gzip
files were read to completion, checking their gzip checksums during extraction.

## Expected annotations and reproduction

[`ensembl116-canonical.tsv`](ensembl116-canonical.tsv) lists the 25 selected
gene IDs and their canonical transcripts. TSS positions come directly from
the transcript start on `+` and end on `-`; expected annotations were not
generated by running genecontext. The structural assertions in
[`test_ensembl.py`](../test_ensembl.py) use explicit exon/CDS intervals and
inclusive gaps between exons from these models.

To recreate the GFF3, select these gene IDs from the full source together
with all their transcript, exon, CDS, and UTR descendants. Retain complete
models, including alternative transcripts. Keep the original metadata and
sequence-region directives for the represented chromosomes, omit unrelated
`biological_region` rows, and sort feature rows by chromosome, numeric start,
numeric end, then the full row in byte order. Do not modify the attributes.

The `processed_transcript` model ENST00000642887 is not tagged canonical.
Its parent ENSG00000285254 has a different, canonical pseudogenic transcript;
the structural tests check that the processed transcript contributes only
when all transcripts are selected.
